note:
Mr Hughes, 74. Annual review.
Known AF, rate controlled on bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD; on apixaban 5 mg BD.
HTN on amlodipine. No history of stroke or TIA.
Plan: continue, bloods in 6 months.

58-year-old woman referred to the AF clinic with intermittent palpitations.
7-day Holter captured her usual palpitations: sinus rhythm with occasional atrial ectopics; no AF recorded.
No previous AF diagnosis. Discharged to GP and reassured.
No regular medication.
rationale: AF appears only as the clinic's name and in 'no AF recorded'; the Holter caught her symptoms in sinus rhythm.

note:
Mrs Okafor, 69. Medication review.
PAF diagnosed on Holter 2021, on edoxaban 60 mg OD.
Ramipril 5 mg for blood pressure, well controlled.
No bleeding problems.
rationale: PAF is paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and ramipril for blood pressure is treated hypertension.

note:
81M, routine BP check with the practice nurse.
Pulse irregularly irregular, rate 96. ?AF
12-lead ECG booked for Thursday.
HTN, T2DM on metformin. Asymptomatic.
rationale: ?AF with the ECG still to be done is suspected AF, not a diagnosis.

note:
Cardiology clinic letter: Mr Bennett, 68.
Persistent AF; DC cardioversion failed in 2025, so now a rate control strategy.
Echo: LVEF 35%, moderately dilated LV. Hypertension on amlodipine.
Continue apixaban 5 mg BD.
No diabetes, stroke, TIA, thromboembolism or vascular disease.
rationale: LVEF 35% is LV systolic dysfunction, which counts as heart failure in CHA2DS2-VASc.

note:
52-year-old woman attending for an NHS Health Check.
Mother had AF and was on warfarin; she is worried she may develop it.
Pulse regular 72, BP 124/78. No palpitations.
No past medical history of note.
rationale: The AF is her mother's diagnosis, not the patient's.

note:
Mr Shah, 63. Review after his procedure.
AF ablated (pulmonary vein isolation) 2019; remains in sinus rhythm.
Continues apixaban on cardiology advice. T2DM, diet controlled.
No history of stroke or TIA.
rationale: A history of AF still counts after ablation, and diet-controlled type 2 diabetes is diabetes.

note:
71-year-old man, cardiology letter.
Typical atrial flutter with 2:1 block on ECG; cavotricuspid isthmus ablation planned.
Started rivaroxaban 20 mg OD pending the procedure.
Hypertension on ramipril.
rationale: Atrial flutter only is outside this audit even though it is anticoagulated.

note:
Mr Doyle, 47. Two days of palpitations.
ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate 130. Rate controlled with bisoprolol.
No hypertension, diabetes, heart failure or vascular disease.
Anticoagulation not offered; echo and TFTs requested.

Mrs Lewis, 77. Results of 7-day Holter (requested for ?AF).
Sinus rhythm throughout; no evidence of atrial fibrillation.
Palpitations likely ectopics. Hypertension, on amlodipine.
No further cardiac investigation planned.
rationale: The suspicion was tested on a Holter and AF was not found.

note:
79F. Paroxysmal AF found on monitoring after a TIA in 2022; on apixaban since.
Today's ECG: sinus rhythm, no AF.
HTN on losartan. No bleeding.
rationale: Paroxysmal AF remains the diagnosis when today's ECG shows sinus rhythm.

note:
Mr Grant, 66. Leg pain on walking 100 yards, relieved by rest.
Claudication, ABPI 0.6 on the right. Referred to vascular surgery.
Pulse regular. Ex-smoker. Started atorvastatin and clopidogrel.
rationale: Claudication with an ABPI of 0.6 is peripheral arterial disease, so vascular is true.

note:
Discharge summary. Mrs Evans, 84.
Admitted with decompensated heart failure (HFrEF, LVEF 30%) and permanent AF with a fast ventricular rate.
Background: HTN, T2DM on insulin, CVA 2020.
Discharged on apixaban, bisoprolol and furosemide.
rationale: CVA (cerebrovascular accident) is a previous stroke.

note:
72-year-old woman seen at the flu clinic.
Pulse noted to be irregularly irregular; no symptoms.
ECG requested; to see GP with the result.
Hypertension on amlodipine.
rationale: An irregularly irregular pulse is a reason to look for AF; until an ECG confirms it, it is suspected.

note:
Mr Ahmed, 70. Cardiology follow-up letter.
AF, DC cardioversion March 2023, remains in sinus rhythm.
NSTEMI 2017 with PCI to LAD. On edoxaban 60 mg OD and atorvastatin.
No diabetes. No history of hypertension.
rationale: AF treated by cardioversion is still a diagnosis of AF, and an NSTEMI is a prior myocardial infarction.

note:
Mrs Ward, 65. ED discharge summary.
Diagnosis: atrial flutter (typical, 2:1 block), not AF.
Cardioverted; sinus rhythm on discharge. Referred for flutter ablation.
Rivaroxaban started. No past medical history.
rationale: The summary names atrial flutter and says it is not AF; flutter alone is outside the audit.

note:
Mr Clarke, 78. Annual AF review.
AF on apixaban 5 mg BD, rate controlled with bisoprolol.
PMH: NSTEMI 2019 (PCI to RCA), PAD with left fem-pop bypass 2021, T2DM on metformin.
No history of hypertension, heart failure, LV systolic dysfunction, stroke, TIA or thromboembolism.
rationale: NSTEMI and PAD are both vascular disease, which scores one point however many conditions there are.

note:
34-year-old woman, 8 weeks postpartum.
Palpitations on standing; pulse regular 104. ECG: sinus tachycardia.
TFTs and FBC requested. No past medical history.

Home visit. Mrs Robinson, 76, housebound.
Known atrial fibrillation; declined anticoagulation in 2024 after discussing the risks.
Hypertension treated with indapamide. Reviewed today: still declines.
No history of stroke or TIA.
rationale: Declining anticoagulation does not remove the diagnosis; she is who the audit is meant to find.

note:
Mr Fraser, 61. Smartwatch notification of an irregular rhythm.
12-lead ECG and 7-day patch monitor: sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopics, including during repeat watch alerts; no AF recorded. No previous AF diagnosis.
T2DM (HbA1c 61) on metformin and gliclazide. HTN on ramipril.
rationale: The watch alerts were investigated with monitoring that caught them in sinus rhythm, and no AF was recorded.

note:
82M. Medication review.
PAF, on rivaroxaban 15 mg OD (CrCl 42).
Left MCA infarct 2018 with mild residual right arm weakness.
Amlodipine 10 mg for BP.
rationale: PAF is paroxysmal AF and a left MCA infarct is a previous stroke.

note:
Mr Byrne, 59. Follow-up after inferior STEMI in 2025 treated with primary PCI.
No angina. Pulse regular. Echo: LVEF 55%.
On aspirin, ticagrelor, atorvastatin, bisoprolol and ramipril.
No hypertension or diabetes.
rationale: Ramipril and bisoprolol are standard after a heart attack, not here for hypertension, and LVEF 55% is normal.

note:
67-year-old woman with episodes of a racing heart lasting minutes.
Examination and ECG today normal, sinus rhythm.
Possible paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: 7-day Holter requested.
Type 2 diabetes on metformin.
rationale: 'Possible' with the Holter still to come is suspected AF, not confirmed.

note:
Discharge summary. 73-year-old woman.
New-onset AF with fast ventricular response; cardioverted with amiodarone, discharged in sinus rhythm.
Edoxaban started; review in 3 months.
Background: hypertension; complex aortic arch plaque on CT.
rationale: A confirmed AF episode followed by sinus rhythm is a history of AF, and aortic plaque counts as vascular disease.

note:
Mr Patel, 80. Clinic letter.
Atrial flutter with variable block, rate controlled; on apixaban.
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%).
No stroke, TIA, diabetes or hypertension.
rationale: Atrial flutter only, so outside this audit despite the DOAC.

note:
Mrs Kowalski, 76. Seen with her daughter about starting anticoagulation.
AF confirmed on ECG last week (rate 88). Asymptomatic.
On amlodipine and ramipril for blood pressure; metformin and sitagliptin for diabetes.
No heart failure, stroke, TIA, thromboembolism or vascular disease. Plan: start apixaban.
rationale: Hypertension and diabetes are given by their treatment, and treated hypertension counts.

note:
Mr Turner, 57. Asks about his stroke risk: his father died of a stroke at 70.
Pulse regular 68. BP 126/80; no history of hypertension. No palpitations.
No history of stroke or TIA. Non-smoker.
rationale: The stroke was his father's, and he has never been diagnosed with hypertension.

note:
Care home review. Mr Hall, 88.
Permanent AF, rate controlled with digoxin. On edoxaban.
Previous TIA 2016. Hypertension. Mild dementia.

Mr Wood, 70. Pre-operative assessment for hip replacement.
Irregular pulse noted: ECG shows sinus rhythm with frequent ventricular ectopics, no AF.
Hypertension on amlodipine. Fit for surgery.
rationale: The irregular pulse is explained by ectopics on the ECG, which shows no AF.

note:
64-year-old woman, arrhythmia clinic letter.
Persistent AF, symptomatic; listed for DC cardioversion.
Rivaroxaban 20 mg OD for at least 3 weeks beforehand.
HTN. Echo: normal LV function.

45M, palpitations after coffee.
ECG: sinus rhythm with atrial ectopics. Thyroid function normal.
Advised to cut down on caffeine. No past medical history.

Mr Murray, 75. Heart failure nurse review.
HFrEF, LVEF 30%, on sacubitril/valsartan, bisoprolol and dapagliflozin.
History of AF, in sinus rhythm since ablation in 2022; remains on apixaban.
No diabetes or hypertension; dapagliflozin is for his heart failure.
rationale: Dapagliflozin is given here for heart failure, not diabetes.

note:
Mr Davies, 72. Paroxysmal AF, now in sinus rhythm on bisoprolol.
On apixaban.
Heart attack 2018, stent to LAD. No hypertension or diabetes.
rationale: The note states paroxysmal AF, so that type is the label although he is now in sinus rhythm; a heart attack is a prior myocardial infarction, so vascular is true.

note:
83-year-old woman, falls clinic.
Pulse irregular on examination; ECG not yet done.
?AF ?ectopics. ECG and bloods booked.
Hypertension on amlodipine. Previous TIA 2019.
rationale: ?AF with the ECG not yet done is suspected AF.

note:
Mrs Green, 81. Stroke review 6 months after a left lacunar infarct.
On clopidogrel and atorvastatin. BP 138/82 on ramipril for hypertension.
T2DM on metformin. Mobilising with a stick.
rationale: Nothing in the note mentions AF, so she is not in the audit however high her score.

note:
Discharge summary. Mr Reid, 69.
Admitted with fast AF (rate 150) and chest tightness; troponin negative.
Rate controlled with bisoprolol; remains in AF at discharge. Edoxaban started.
Background: claudication (ABPI 0.6), ex-smoker.
rationale: Claudication with an ABPI of 0.6 is peripheral arterial disease, so vascular is true.

note:
Mrs Ali, 74. AFL ablated 2020, no recurrence on annual ECG.
Still on apixaban: asks whether it can stop.
T2DM on metformin. No hypertension.
rationale: AFL is atrial flutter, and no atrial fibrillation is recorded.

note:
Mr Lowe, 60. Smartwatch has sent several irregular rhythm notifications.
Pulse regular in surgery today; ECG sinus rhythm.
14-day patch monitor requested. Hypertension on amlodipine.
rationale: Watch alerts with monitoring still pending are suspected AF.

note:
Mrs Hill, 86. Annual review.
AF 2015, cardioverted; in sinus rhythm on every ECG since. Remains on apixaban.
Heart failure (LVEF 40%), hypertension, T2DM. Previous NSTEMI 2018.
rationale: LVEF 40% counts as LV systolic dysfunction, and NSTEMI is a prior myocardial infarction.

note:
Mrs Young, 48. ABPM after a high clinic reading: daytime average 128/79.
Hypertension not confirmed; no treatment. Recheck in 5 years.
No palpitations; pulse regular.
rationale: Ambulatory monitoring did not confirm hypertension, so hypertension is false.

note:
Ms Novak, 38. Persistent AF for 8 months, awaiting ablation.
On flecainide. Anticoagulation discussed; not started.
No other medical history.
